subject: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

From: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightCart's finance team sent over the sample invoice and we have two items that need clarification before legal will sign. High-level: (1) how context-length prorating interacts with our 500k token monthly seat bundle, and (2) the rounding rule when a streaming invocation ends mid-token (we're seeing fractional tokens on the sample).

Attached is the CSV extract from our test invoice (brightcart_sample_invoice_line.csv). Specific asks:
- Can you show a line-by-line reconciliation that maps our API calls to invoice lines under the bundle + per-token overage model?
- If we run long-context chats (25k messages history) that frequently exceed the 16k sequence window, will we be double-charged (bundle + per-call long-context premium)?
- We noted a rounding behavior where a few calls showed 0.5 token values — what's the real billing quantum?

Would appreciate a clear example (3–4 sample API calls, math shown) and whether Redwood will make any rounding concessions for pilot customers.

Thanks,
Jordan
Director, Platform Eng — BrightCart
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

Jordan — thanks for the CSV and clear asks. Quick summary up front:
1) Bundle (seat) covers baseline per-token usage up to the committed monthly units. Overages are per-token. We do not charge a separate "long-context premium" on top of per-token overage; long context increases token counts (through more input tokens and KV state) which consumes bundle units or produces overage.
2) Rounding: we meter at the subtoken level during inference but invoice rounding is to a 1-token granularity after aggregation per invoice line. For small fractional artifacts on the CSV I suspect pre-aggregation exports. I'll reconcile with billing export team.

I'll provide an explicit 3-call worked example showing: how tokens map to bundle units, how partial-token artifacts are aggregated and rounded, and how calls that require a 32k model (for sequences >16k) are billed if model substitution occurs. Ben / Soojin — can you help with a short reconciliation and a recommended wording for the contract that prevents double-billing confusion?

Priya
Senior Manager, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

PRIORITY: draft sample math below (feel free to paste into reply to BrightCart)

Example calls (BrightCart test):
1) Short chat: 2 prompts (system + user), response 350 tokens. Metering: 380 input tokens + 350 output = 730 tokens. Invoice: consumes 730 bundle units.
2) Long-history single-turn: 24k history trimmed to 14k prefix + current prompt 1.2k -> input 15.2k tokens, output 800 tokens. If the session requires model with 32k support we substitute model-x-32k; billing: total tokens = 15,200 + 800 = 16,000 tokens. Consumes 16k bundle units (or overage if bundle exhausted). No extra per-call "long-context surcharge".
3) Streaming partial-token case: client observes 0.5 token in export because exporter recorded incremental subtoken emission. Real billing: we accumulate all subtoken increments for the invoice period and round to nearest token per-line. So three small calls totalling 2.6 tokens would be billed as 3 tokens after aggregation.

Rounding rule to propose in contract: "Monthly metered usage will be aggregated per invoice line and rounded up to the nearest whole token. Subtoken-level metering is used for internal accuracy but will not cause fractional token charges on invoices."

Attachment: sample reconciliation CSV (I reworked your extract) and a one-line clause. Soojin — confirm the aggregation + invoice export timeframe and whether we can commit to 'round-up' vs 'nearest'.

-Ben
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 Jun 2028 09:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

Confirming billing export behavior:
- Metering layer records fractional (subtoken) increments at call time.
- The billing pipeline aggregates usage per customer per SKU per monthly window, then applies token quantum rounding. Our standard is to round up to the next whole token on invoice lines (we'll show math).
- For model substitution (e.g., 16k -> 32k), we only charge the token counts consumed by the higher-capacity model; no additional model-capacity premium. If BrightCart requests forced model pinning to avoid substitution, they can, but that is a configuration choice (may affect latency/cost).

I attached a small reconciliation example (brightcart_sample_invoice_line.csv) that maps three API traces to invoice lines and shows aggregation:
- API trace A: 730 tokens -> invoice line A: 730
- API trace B: 16,000 tokens -> invoice line B: 16,000
- API trace C: three micro-streams totalling 2.6 tokens -> invoice line C: 3 (rounded up)

Pilot concession ask: finance is open to offering BrightCart a one-month "rounding buffer" that offsets up to 50 tokens of aggregated fractional drift for their first invoice after go-live (to avoid small surprise charges). This would appear as a one-time credit on the invoice. Ben / Karthik — is that OK?

-Soojin
From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@brightcart.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify: packaging tiers vs. context-prorate + sample invoice line

Jordan — thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps: 
1) No double-billing: bundle covers tokens; long-context increases token counts but we don't apply a second "long-context premium".
2) Rounding: invoice lines round up to the nearest whole token after aggregation. Subtoken artifacts in exports are expected; your CSV now reconciles to invoice-friendly integers (attached).
3) Pilot concession: we will provide a one-time invoice credit up to 50 tokens to cover fractional drift on your first invoice post-launch. We'll document the rounding rule in contract language as Soojin suggested.

Attached: reconciled CSV (brightcart_sample_invoice_line.csv) and suggested contract wording (proposal_pricing_matrix.xlsx). Please confirm if BrightCart wants model pinning for any routes or if substitution is acceptable; pinning may increase cost. Once you confirm, I'll loop legal to add the rounding clause and the pilot credit into the SOW.

Best,
Priya
